headline: Finishing Your Basement: 5 Costly Moisture and Layout Mistakes to Avoid
articleBody:
Finishing a basement delivers fantastic square footage, but below-grade environments present unique moisture, framing, and code hurdles. Avoiding these five frequent missteps protects your investment and keeps your home comfortable year-round.

Common Mistakes to Avoid
1. Covering Up Moisture Problems: Never frame or insulate over damp foundation walls or active seepage. Trapping water behind vapor barriers leads to hidden mold growth and ruined drywall. All leaks must be corrected on the outside or inside before framing begins.
2. Forgetting Emergency Egress: If your plan includes a bedroom, local building codes mandate an openable emergency escape and rescue window with specific dimensions and adequate window-well clearance. Skipping this prevents permits from passing and creates serious safety hazards.
3. Boxed-In Mechanical Access: Framing walls too close to your furnace, water heater, or main water shutoff creates a nightmare for routine maintenance. Always leave required service clearances and access doors.
4. Hanging Drywall Before Rough Inspections: Rushing to close up walls before framing, electrical, plumbing, and HVAC passes rough municipal inspection can lead to inspectors ordering you to tear down fresh drywall at your expense.
5. Direct Wood-to-Concrete Contact: Fastening standard framing lumber directly against cold, damp concrete foundations causes premature rot. Treated sill plates and proper thermal insulation barriers are non-negotiable.
